description: Make the c3 Memory Trial map-counting challenge reliable by remembering the game_map the first time any tool sees it and recalling it when the count question omits the map. Root cause: memoryquestion._handle_count returns _err(400, 'Missing game_map') when no map is passed, but the c3 challenge text never includes the map (it is only presented once at game start via pathfinding). The supervisor therefore calls count with no map, gets a 400 every time, and retries in a loop (~9 calls observed) until the challenge fails and a life is lost. Fix uses approach A (auto-persist + fallback): persist the map into the module-level _memory_store whenever memoryquestion sees one, expose an explicit store-map path, make _handle_count fall back to the remembered map, and update the supervisor + memoryquestion prompts so the agent stores the map at game start and does NOT retry a failing count. This is a single coherent unit of work. Do NOT touch door/key transform rules or routing.
steps: In memoryquestion.py, define a well-known constant for the remembered-map key, e.g. GAME_MAP_KEY = 'game_map' (module level near _memory_store).

Add a helper _remember_map(game_map) that, given a non-empty list-of-lists game_map, stores a copy into _memory_store[GAME_MAP_KEY]. Add _recall_map() returning _memory_store.get(GAME_MAP_KEY). Keep them small and pure so they are easy to unit test.

In lambda_handler, after body is parsed, auto-persist any incoming map: if body.get('game_map') is a non-empty list, call _remember_map(game_map) BEFORE action dispatch. This means count/store/any call that carries a map updates the remembered map. This is the resilient auto-persist path.

Add an explicit action 'store_map' (dispatched in lambda_handler) so the supervisor can store the map at game start with {"action":"store_map","game_map":[[...]]}. Implement _handle_store_map(body): validate game_map is a non-empty list, call _remember_map, return {'success': true, 'rows': R, 'cols': C, 'total_cells': N} (do NOT echo the full map back - it wastes tokens). Return _err(400, ...) for a missing/empty map. Update the lambda_handler docstring action list and the action-routing comment to include store_map.

In _handle_count(body): read game_map = body.get('game_map', []); if it is empty/falsy, fall back to game_map = _recall_map() or []. Keep the existing jagged-row padding and the existing behaviour when a map IS passed. Preserve backward compatibility: existing tests pass a map and must still work identically (breakdown, answer, dimensions, question_ids_found unchanged).

When _handle_count has no map from either source, keep failing cleanly with a clear _err(400, ...) message (e.g. 'No game_map available: none passed and none remembered from game start') so the agent gets a deterministic failure rather than looping. Do not change the HTTP contract shape ({'statusCode':400,'body':json.dumps({'error':...})}).

Update supervisor_system_prompt.txt: (a) add a MemoryQuestion(action="store_map", game_map) tool line; (b) in ROUTING, add a rule that at game start when the map is presented, in addition to Pathfinding, store the map via MemoryQuestion store_map so it can be recalled later (keep the change minimal and consistent with the terse style); (c) update the 'Count tiles on a map -> MemoryQuestion count' rule to note the map is remembered from game start so count needs no game_map, and add an explicit anti-loop instruction: if a count call returns an error, do NOT repeat the identical call - answer 0 or move on rather than retrying the same failing request. Do NOT alter any door/key/refusal/intake rules.

Update memoryquestion_system_prompt.txt: document the store_map action ({"action":"store_map","game_map":[[...]]}) and note that count recalls the remembered map when game_map is omitted; add the same 'never retry an identical failing call' guidance. Keep the terse one-liner-per-action style. Do NOT alter door/key transform documentation.

Add unit tests in tests/test_agent.py. Add a new TestCase class (e.g. TestMemoryMapRecall) with setUp that clears memoryquestion._memory_store. Cover: (1) map-not-passed-but-remembered: store a map via store_map (or via an earlier count call that carried the map), then call count with question only and assert the correct answer/breakdown; (2) no-map-ever: clear store, call count with question only and no map, assert an 'error' key is returned (clean failure, not a crash); (3) store_map returns success with correct rows/cols/total_cells and does NOT echo the full map; (4) multi-type addition when map is remembered: e.g. 'how many c1 + c8?' returns the summed total with correct breakdown; (5) backward compat: count with a map passed still works even if a DIFFERENT map is remembered (passed map takes precedence) - and auto-persist updates the remembered map to the passed one.

Add a new v10 entry at the TOP of CHANGELOG.md (above v9) describing the c3 map-recall fix: the loop/root cause, approach A (auto-persist + store_map + count fallback), prompt updates (store map at game start, no-retry guidance), and 'N tests pass' where N is the new total after adding tests.
